## Purpose
This is to point to the torch stable ABI branch of DeepGEMM (not yet merged upstream, see https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/21). This is "stacked" on top of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48962 with the only difference being the git tag and removing DeepGEMM from the `ALLOWED_UNSTABLE_LIBRARIES` list in `check-torch-abi.py` CI check  (see the last 2 commits).  

This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM


## Test Plan
```
  python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py
```

## Test Result
tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py - PASS
tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py - 100 failed, 322 passed, all failures are fatal error: sanitizer/asan_interface.h: No such file or directory. Not related to TORCH_LIBRARY migration
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py - 16 Passes, 3 failures due to not running SM100 or SM120
tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py - PASS
tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py - PASS


---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

Migration progress using the Audit Python extension [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/):
```
 -- extensions --
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=88, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _deepselect_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=40, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashkda_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=43, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=66, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_extension_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=72, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _qutlass_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] cumem_allocator.abi3.so
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] fs_io_C.abi3.so
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] spinloop.abi3.so
--> [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] third_party/deep_gemm/_C_extension.abi3.so  (stable_shim=78, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa2_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=69, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa3_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
```
Making vLLM completely torch ABI stable!!!


## Performance Benchmarks
Link to performance benchmarks: https://github.com/cleonard530/Benchmarks/pull/1
The tldr; most gemm kernels stayed the same ~~except the `fp8_fp4_gemm_{nn,nt,tn,tt}` kernels which had a 10-20% runtime increase (2-6 µs/call). I ran another workload with them in a vLLM-like workload. In eager mode the regression was about the same, but it disappeared with the CUDA-graph run.~~ the runtime increase in `fp8_fp4_gemm_{nn,nt,tt}` went away when the data element_size was cached. `fp8_fp4_gemm_tn` still has a slight runtime regression, but doesn't seem to be used by vLLM.

With this, vLLM cuda wheel is now ABI stable! 🤩🤩🤩🤩🤩

thank you @Harry-Chen @cleonard530!

Post-merge CI found a hardware-profile compatibility regression in the new DeepGEMM pin.

Main build 94505, H200 MIG 35GB Basic Models Extra Initialization Shard 8, fails `HYV4ForCausalLM` before model initialization:

- agent slice: H200 MIG with **26 SMs** (`h200-ci-2-20`, MIG `1g.35gb`)
- vendored import: `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm._C.init()`
- failure: `_balance_sm_locality_domains()` computes 13 TPCs and hits `assert num_tpcs % 2 == 0`
- vLLM then reports `Sparse Attention Indexer CUDA op requires DeepGEMM support`

The exact same HYV4 test passed in mains 94501 and 94503 on the 16-SM H200 MIG pool. The old pin `6ce1c5e` delegated locality-domain balancing to the extension; the new stable-ABI pin `a981d8e` calls the Python implementation during import, exposing the odd-TPC assertion.

Evidence: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94505#01a135d8-c88b-4377-8c53-0d5e98f47085

This is deterministic for the 26-SM slice, so a retry on the same pool will not help. The durable fix is to make DeepGEMM's locality balancing support an odd TPC count (or safely disable balancing on that topology), then bump the vLLM pin and validate this exact 26-SM H200 MIG lane. The merged kernel-fusion PR in 94505 is unrelated.
@cleonard530 does your new PR fix what @khluu called out ^ https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61445

@janeyx99 and @khluu, I'm looking into this now.

cc @Harry-Chen

@khluu I opened a new PR on DeepGEMM that should fix this issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/35. `locality_domain.hpp` had a lot of torch api calls that didn't have stable equivalents, and since they were short one time calls, I thought hey could be moved to python, but that caused other issues like you saw. I updated it so that `locality_domain.hpp` looks a lot more like the legacy code, with stable wrappers to handle the unstable APIs. 

Note, the underlying balancing issue is still present, as it was in the legacy code. Restoring lazy initialization means it no longer surfaces during import; it is reached only when a caller requests the balanced SM locality domains, directly or through an API such as `release_mlopart()`.
FYI we reverted this to unblock CI for now: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61510

## Purpose
This is to point to the torch stable ABI branch of DeepGEMM (not yet merged upstream, see https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/21). This is "stacked" on top of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48962 with the only difference being the git tag and removing DeepGEMM from the `ALLOWED_UNSTABLE_LIBRARIES` list in `check-torch-abi.py` CI check  (see the last 2 commits).  

This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM


## Test Plan
```
  python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py
```

## Test Result
tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py - PASS
tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py - 100 failed, 322 passed, all failures are fatal error: sanitizer/asan_interface.h: No such file or directory. Not related to TORCH_LIBRARY migration
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py - 16 Passes, 3 failures due to not running SM100 or SM120
tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py - PASS
tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py - PASS


---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

Migration progress using the Audit Python extension [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/):
```
 -- extensions --
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=88, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _deepselect_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=40, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashkda_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=43, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=66, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_extension_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=72, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _qutlass_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] cumem_allocator.abi3.so
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] fs_io_C.abi3.so
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] spinloop.abi3.so
--> [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] third_party/deep_gemm/_C_extension.abi3.so  (stable_shim=78, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa2_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=69, unstable=0)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa3_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=63, unstable=0)
```
Making vLLM completely torch ABI stable!!!


## Performance Benchmarks
Link to performance benchmarks: https://github.com/cleonard530/Benchmarks/pull/1
The tldr; most gemm kernels stayed the same ~~except the `fp8_fp4_gemm_{nn,nt,tn,tt}` kernels which had a 10-20% runtime increase (2-6 µs/call). I ran another workload with them in a vLLM-like workload. In eager mode the regression was about the same, but it disappeared with the CUDA-graph run.~~ the runtime increase in `fp8_fp4_gemm_{nn,nt,tt}` went away when the data element_size was cached. `fp8_fp4_gemm_tn` still has a slight runtime regression, but doesn't seem to be used by vLLM.

Post-merge CI found a hardware-profile compatibility regression in the new DeepGEMM pin.

Main build 94505, H200 MIG 35GB Basic Models Extra Initialization Shard 8, fails `HYV4ForCausalLM` before model initialization:

- agent slice: H200 MIG with **26 SMs** (`h200-ci-2-20`, MIG `1g.35gb`)
- vendored import: `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm._C.init()`
- failure: `_balance_sm_locality_domains()` computes 13 TPCs and hits `assert num_tpcs % 2 == 0`
- vLLM then reports `Sparse Attention Indexer CUDA op requires DeepGEMM support`

The exact same HYV4 test passed in mains 94501 and 94503 on the 16-SM H200 MIG pool. The old pin `6ce1c5e` delegated locality-domain balancing to the extension; the new stable-ABI pin `a981d8e` calls the Python implementation during import, exposing the odd-TPC assertion.

Evidence: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94505#01a135d8-c88b-4377-8c53-0d5e98f47085

This is deterministic for the 26-SM slice, so a retry on the same pool will not help. The durable fix is to make DeepGEMM's locality balancing support an odd TPC count (or safely disable balancing on that topology), then bump the vLLM pin and validate this exact 26-SM H200 MIG lane. The merged kernel-fusion PR in 94505 is unrelated.
